# The Moon's Quiet Constancy

## Scripture
"He set the moon for seasons; the sun knows its going down." — Psalm 104:19 (WEB)

## Reflection

The moon never hurries. It doesn't panic when clouds roll in, doesn't demand attention when Venus outshines it. It simply takes its place in the turning—waxing and waning, full and hidden, yet always present. Perhaps that's why God hung it in our sky as a calendar of grace.

There are seasons of our faith that feel like a full moon—bright, certain, seen by all. There are seasons that feel like a new moon—dark, empty, as if God has gone silent. But here's the wonder: the moon doesn't change because we can't see it. It remains in orbit, held by a gravity stronger than our perception.

Your present season—whether luminous or hidden—is not a failure of God's faithfulness. It's a phase of His design. The same Lord who set the moon for seasons has set you in this exact moment for a purpose only He fully comprehends. You don't need to manufacture brightness. You only need to remain in orbit, trusting the One who holds you.

The moon teaches us that constancy matters more than consistency. Faithfulness isn't about shining every night—it's about staying in place, awaiting the light.

## Prayer

Faithful Creator, thank You for the moon's quiet witness. When I feel hidden or dim, remind me that You see me fully and hold me steady. Teach me to trust the season You have set for me. Amen.
